# linux_directory (Resource)

Manages a directory, its permissions and ownership. An existing directory is adopted as is.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "linux_directory" "app" {
  path  = "/opt/app/releases"
  mode  = "0750"
  owner = "app"
  group = "app"

  # Delete the directory and its content on destroy.
  force_destroy = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `path` (String) Absolute path of the directory.

### Optional

- `create_parents` (Boolean) Create missing parent directories, like `mkdir -p`. They are not removed with the directory. Defaults to `true`.
- `force_destroy` (Boolean) On destroy, delete the directory with everything it contains. Otherwise destroying fails when the directory is not empty. Defaults to `false`.
- `group` (String) Group, as a group name or GID. Defaults to the primary group of the user running the commands.
- `mode` (String) Permissions, in octal. Defaults to `0755`.
- `owner` (String) Owner, as a user name or UID. Defaults to the user running the commands.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Path of the directory.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The ID is the path of the directory.
terraform import linux_directory.app /opt/app/releases
```
